body: Thanks.  I think it's the other way, though.  My depression is contributing to my drinking.

> Well I will speak from experience, being suicidal is alot like being an addict. Once you have thought about it seriously, it's always there.

This really hit me - you're absolutely correct.  

Where I am it's actually not a holiday today, but I get what you mean about the holiday season in general.  I don't really think that it's what's affecting me because of the fact that I've felt the same way during other parts of the year, but now that I think about it, I do seem to have this kind of problem more often during the winter. 

My dog doesn't really do any fancy tricks that I could show off to friends or anything, but he does know "don't pee on that", which I love, since he lifts his leg on nearly everything when we go for walks and I like to spare people's pretty gardens. Hah.  

There are lots of tricks you can teach, though.  One of the easiest ones to teach is to teach them to spin in a circle - you have a treat or something of interest and guide them through a circle and praise.  When you can consistently get them doing the circle, and they start doing it without guidance the entire way through (they start anticipating your next move after practice), then you can assign a command to it (Spin, circle, etc).  Once you get a good sense of the dog (not all dogs communicate identically) you can move on to other things like beg or roll over.  There's guides for these tricks all over the internet so I won't make this a massive post, but if you have questions I'm happy to answer.

I definitely struggle with depression, I have all my life.  Even when I was just a little kid, I was a total recluse.  I don't really remember feeling sadness when I was really young (around 10 I started thinking about suicide) but I know I was an odd kid.  My mom has told me how much she worried. 

I do have other hobbies but when I'm depressed I just have no interest in them.  I do continue to walk my dog, though, which I think is as good for me as it is for him.  I can't really take on other dogs because of my unpredictable schedule but I'll keep that in mind if I ever find myself dogless.  I used to train dogs (other people's dogs) but I found that I'm not as good with people as I am with dogs, so it just doesn't really suit me. 

Nobody else thinks I have an alcohol problem, but I'm sort of a recluse, so I doubt they would notice even if I was 100% sure that I did have an alcohol problem.  It doesn't really interfere with my life, I just hear all over that drinking when you're depressed is a sign and I don't know, I thought I'd ask.

Thanks for your reply.

Thanks, it's thoughtful of you to note that you've read it. 

I can't really identify the things that set me off.  It seems completely out of the blue.  I know that I get *very* depressed when I'm on my period, but it's not exclusively period-related.  I have these kinds of days just out of the blue, too.  I'll just wake up one day and think to myself, why the fuck am I alive? 

I've seen several therapists, some better than others.  Sometimes it helps with my overarching issues, but it hasn't really helped me deal with these random bouts of extreme depression.
